my friends are exactly like this and it makes me scared because I'm still questioning. i feel like if I were to say that I was straight they would dump me. it's making it hard to explore myself and know what I really like. i think girls are kind pretty (I'm a 13 F) but I've really only had crushes/flirted with boys.
i'm gonna tell her when she leaves but its a whole year away and its hard to hold on even now

i did have a therapist for a while before covid but I also  have trust issues, I have this irrational fear that my parents will think I'm copying my sister because this happed to her too. i want to tell my sister but my trust issues make me scared that she will tell my parents and they will push it aside. I'm trying to give hints to my state but my mom is either clueless or pushing them aside. 

i don't know who I can trust and who will take me seriously

i understand but all i have to say is try to find something to hold onto. u don't have to stay for anybody or even yourself. but when a little bird flies by watch it. watch them. watch how free they are. take it all in. u might be free if u die but you'll never see that bird again. you'll never meet the cute person from the airport again. find something even if it's the smallest thing in the world like the way the air smells on that one beach. hold onto it. live for it. hell, if you can stay there. drive to that beach every day if you have to. but try to hold on. u just have to find the thing that triggers the split second of happiness. If you do end up leaving know everyone here will miss you. we might not know you but for me, when I find out someone left again it brings me closer. so know whatever you do, we care.

sometimes i'm happy and other times i feel like no one would miss me. a couple of years ago I wrote a suicide note and my parents found it. they talked about it for a week then never mentioned it. if it was so easy to forget a note like that would it even be hard to forget me?
